title: Keep the selection visible after a wrapped-line resize

messages.text: When I resize a narrow window, the cursor can land below the viewport after wrapping recalculates. Please trace it and make the selection remain visible. Keep the update flow deterministic.
I’ll reproduce it first, then trace the resize and selection paths before changing geometry.

tools.name: rg
tools.label: Locate resize and selection handlers
tools.output:
src/update/editor_navigation.rs:88: ensure_selection_visible
src/view/editor_viewport.rs:141: relayout_after_resize
src/view/editor_text.rs:302: selection_rect

messages.text: Context compacted. Preserve the user’s viewport invariant and existing dirty work.
The smallest reproduction is a long Markdown line with soft wrap, then drag the width smaller while the caret is near its end.
That points at stale visual-row geometry rather than the logical cursor position.

tools.name: read_file
tools.label: Read viewport relayout
tools.output: relayout_after_resize updates wrap cache, then returns before ensure_selection_visible runs.

messages.text: The current code measures the caret against rows from before the new width is applied.
Please avoid another local line loop. The shared visual-row traversal should remain the source of truth.
Agreed. I found an existing traversal helper used by hit testing.

tools.name: read_file
tools.label: Inspect shared visual rows
tools.output: visual_rows_for_range(document, wrap_cache, range) yields rendered rows and y extents.

messages.text: I’ll use that helper after relayout and make the resulting scroll delta a command.
There is also a performance concern: do not scan the whole document during a resize.
The helper can start at the current viewport range. I’ll expand only until it sees the selected visual row.

tools.name: rg
tools.label: Find viewport range helper
tools.output:
src/view/editor_layout.rs:71: visible_row_window
src/view/hit_testing.rs:46: visual_rows_in_viewport

messages.text: I have a narrow change path: invalidate wrapping, rebuild the visible row window, resolve selection geometry, then emit scrolling if needed.
Before editing, check whether image and CSV tabs can reach this route.
I’m checking the caller gate.

tools.name: read_file
tools.label: Inspect resize dispatch
tools.output: Editor resize handler is entered for all tabs; text layout work is only guarded in one later branch.

messages.text: The fast path needs an early EditorState::is_plain_text_mode() guard. I’ll preserve the existing special-tab handling.
Good. Could you ask a subagent to check for existing viewport invariants or tests we should reuse?
I delegated a read-only test inventory.

tools.label: Inspect existing viewport tests
tools.input: {task:'find viewport and wrapped selection test coverage'}
tools.output: Started subagent session demo-codex-split-layout.

messages.text: Meanwhile I’ll write the reproduction as a test before changing the update path.
Use the native fixture style. The issue only occurs after the second resize, from wide to narrow.
Captured: start wide, select at the tail of a wrapped line, resize twice, then assert the caret rectangle intersects the viewport.

tools.name: write_patch
tools.label: Add failing wrapped-selection test
tools.output: Added one deterministic fixture-driven test.

messages.text: The test is intentionally failing on the current revision.
Show me the failure before you patch the behavior.

tools.name: just test-one
tools.label: Run new viewport test
tools.output:
FAILED tests/editor_viewport_follow_selection.rs:41
assertion failed: selection_rect(&editor).intersects(editor.viewport())
selection y=688..708, viewport y=0..512

messages.text: That is the bug. Please make scrolling happen after the width-dependent layout is stable, not from the runtime directly.
I’ll add an update message carrying the completed layout revision and calculate the offset in the deterministic update handler.

tools.name: write_patch
tools.label: Move follow-selection into update
tools.output: Updated messages, commands, resize dispatch, viewport layout, and selection geometry.

messages.text: The code now resolves the selection against the post-wrap cache and only walks visible rows plus the selection’s row.
Does that create a loop when scrolling itself triggers another layout?
The message includes a layout revision; an already-handled revision returns no command. I’ll add a regression test for that path.

tools.name: just test-one
tools.label: Run viewport tests
tools.output: 2 passed, 0 failed

messages.text: Please test a selection above the viewport too, and test an image tab does not enter text code.
Adding both cases now.

tools.name: write_patch
tools.label: Add boundary and special-tab tests
tools.output: Added upward scroll and image-tab guard coverage.

messages.text: Subagent report: existing tests assert viewport clamping but did not cover a wrap-cache invalidation between selection calculation and scroll. The new fixture fills that gap.
Nice. I’m worried the perf stage is missing, because this is a resize cost we’ll want to see in the F2 overlay.
I’ll extend the shared perf stage list rather than adding a local timer.

tools.name: write_patch
tools.label: Instrument shared layout stage
tools.output: Added selection_visibility_after_layout to the existing editor layout stage group.

messages.text: The new stage is visible with other editor layout timing and remains inactive unless the selection needs inspection.
Run formatting and the relevant test group. If something fails, show the raw output rather than summarising it.

messages.text: Formatting caught a missing comma in the new command match. I’ll make that mechanical correction and rerun.
Okay. Also, avoid showing irrelevant formatting churn in the eventual diff.

messages.text: The formatter only changed the new match arm and wrapping in the test fixture.
Can you capture a native screenshot at a narrow width? I want to see the selected text and scrollbar together.

tools.output: Token started with fixture. Window resized to 320px.

messages.text: The caret stays just inside the lower padding after the second resize. I’m going to inspect a high-DPI case before calling it done.
Please include 125% scale and a line with syntax highlighting. The height can differ from plain Markdown.

tools.name: run_fixture

tools.output:
selection visible after resize
layout revision: 19
scroll delta: 196px

messages.text: The high-DPI case passes. The shared row geometry keeps highlighted and plain text on the same path.
One more thing: could a stale command from the first resize scroll after the second resize?
I found that the runtime can deliver the first resize command late. The revision guard drops it, but the test did not model that ordering.

tools.name: write_patch
tools.label: Add stale layout command test

messages.text: Great. Could the screenshot stay as verification output only? It should not become a repository asset.
